nodes.text: Let $n$ be sufficiently large. Is there some choice of congruence class $a_p$ for all primes $2\leq p\leq n$ such that every integer in $[1,n]$ satisfies at least two of the congruences $\equiv a_p\pmod{p}$?

#689 : [Er79d] [Er80,p.108] number theory One can ask a similar question replacing $2$ by any fixed integer $r$ (provided $n$ is sufficiently large depending on $r$). See also [687] and [688] . If we replace primes with all integers then this is [1205] . This problem (with $2$ replaced by $10$) is Problem 45 on Green's open problems list .
